note: Physics/Chemistry/Biology round 2 (verified calculations, experiment-based items) + bank-wide retirement of one-line recall stems in every subject.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student measures the length of a pencil five times and obtains 12.1 cm, 12.3 cm, 12.2 cm, 12.2 cm and 12.2 cm. The best estimate of the length is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The unit of power expressed in fundamental units is
questions.explanation: Power = energy/time; energy = force × distance = (kg m s⁻²)(m) = kg m² s⁻²; dividing by s gives kg m² s⁻³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy walks 3 km east and then 4 km north. His displacement from the starting point is
questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line distance: √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km (north-east of the start).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act on a body at right angles to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is
questions.explanation: Resultant = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car travelling at 30 m/s is brought to rest by its brakes in a distance of 90 m. The deceleration is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object thrown vertically upwards returns to the thrower after 4 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the initial speed was
questions.explanation: Time to the top = 2 s; v = u − gt ⇒ 0 = u − 10(2) ⇒ u = 20 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A train accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s over a distance of 400 m. The time taken is
questions.explanation: Average velocity = (10 + 30)/2 = 20 m/s; t = s/v_avg = 400/20 = 20 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform metre rule is balanced at the 40 cm mark when a mass of 20 g hangs at the 10 cm mark. The mass of the rule is
questions.explanation: Weight of the rule acts at 50 cm. Moments about 40 cm: 20 × 30 = M × 10 ⇒ M = 60 g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 5 kg block rests on a rough horizontal surface. If the coefficient of static friction is 0.4 and g = 10 m/s², the minimum horizontal force needed to start it moving is
questions.explanation: Limiting friction F = μR = 0.4 × (5 × 10) = 20 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone of mass 2 kg falls from a height of 20 m. Taking g = 10 m/s² and ignoring air resistance, its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground is
questions.explanation: All potential energy becomes kinetic: mgh = 2 × 10 × 20 = 400 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pump lifts 200 kg of water through 15 m every minute. Taking g = 10 m/s², the power of the pump is
questions.explanation: Work per minute = mgh = 200 × 10 × 15 = 30,000 J; power = 30,000/60 = 500 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A gun of mass 5 kg fires a bullet of mass 20 g at 400 m/s. The recoil velocity of the gun is
questions.explanation: Momentum conserved: 5 × v = 0.02 × 400 ⇒ v = 8/5 = 1.6 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inclined plane 5 m long is used to raise a load through a height of 1 m. Its velocity ratio is
questions.explanation: VR of an inclined plane = length of slope/height = 5/1 = 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block and tackle with 4 pulleys is used to lift a load of 600 N with an effort of 200 N. Its efficiency is
questions.explanation: VR = 4 (number of pulleys); MA = 600/200 = 3; efficiency = 3/4 × 100 = 75%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire of length 2 m is stretched by 4 mm when a load of 40 N hangs from it. The load required to stretch a similar wire of the same length by 6 mm is
questions.explanation: Hooke's law: force ∝ extension ⇒ F = 40 × 6/4 = 60 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body weighs 50 N in air and 30 N when completely immersed in water. The upthrust on the body is
questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight in air − weight in water = 50 − 30 = 20 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body weighs 50 N in air and 30 N in water. The relative density of the body is
questions.explanation: Relative density = weight in air/upthrust in water = 50/(50 − 30) = 2.5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hydraulic press has pistons of area 10 cm² and 500 cm². A force of 40 N on the small piston produces a force on the large piston of
questions.explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally: F₂ = F₁ × A₂/A₁ = 40 × 500/10 = 2,000 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metal rod 2.000 m long at 0 °C becomes 2.002 m long at 100 °C. Its linear expansivity is
questions.explanation: α = ΔL/(L₀Δθ) = 0.002/(2 × 100) = 1 × 10⁻⁵ per kelvin.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 0.2 kg of water at 80 °C is mixed with 0.3 kg of water at 30 °C. Ignoring heat losses, the final temperature of the mixture is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1 kW electric kettle takes 2 minutes to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 25 °C. The energy wasted is (specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg K)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The temperature of a body is 27 °C. On the kelvin scale this is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance between two successive crests of a water wave is 20 cm and 5 crests pass a point every second. The speed of the wave is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radio station broadcasts at a frequency of 100 MHz. Taking the speed of radio waves as 3 × 10⁸ m/s, the wavelength is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stretched string of length 50 cm vibrates in its fundamental mode with a frequency of 200 Hz. If the length is reduced to 25 cm at the same tension, the new fundamental frequency is
questions.explanation: For a fixed tension f ∝ 1/L; halving the length doubles the frequency: 400 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ship sends a sound pulse to the sea bed and receives the echo 3 s later. If the speed of sound in water is 1500 m/s, the depth of the sea is
questions.explanation: Distance travelled = 1500 × 3 = 4500 m, there and back ⇒ depth = 2250 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms a real image 30 cm from the mirror. The object distance is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object 2 cm tall is placed 20 cm from a converging lens of focal length 15 cm. The magnification of the image is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of light in a glass of refractive index 1.5 is (speed in air = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person cannot see objects clearly beyond 2 m. The defect and the lens needed to correct it are
questions.explanation: Inability to see distant objects is short sight (myopia), corrected with a diverging (concave) lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel and the combination is connected in series with a 4 Ω resistor. The total resistance is
questions.explanation: Parallel: 6/3 = 2 Ω; series with 4 Ω gives 2 + 4 = 6 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a 2.5 Ω resistor. The current in the circuit is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω drives a current of 0.5 A through an external resistor. The terminal p.d. of the cell is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire of resistance 8 Ω is stretched until its length doubles (volume unchanged). Its new resistance is
questions.explanation: Doubling the length halves the area; R ∝ L/A ⇒ R becomes 8 × 2 × 2 = 32 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four 100 W bulbs are used for 5 hours a day for 30 days. The energy consumed is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in parallel across a 10 V supply. The total charge stored is
questions.explanation: Parallel: C = 2 + 3 = 5 μF; Q = CV = 5 × 10 = 50 μC.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer steps 240 V down to 12 V and delivers 2 A to a lamp. Assuming 100% efficiency, the current in the primary coil is
questions.explanation: Power in = power out: 240 × Iₚ = 12 × 2 ⇒ Iₚ = 24/240 = 0.1 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnet is pushed into a coil connected to a galvanometer and the needle deflects to the right. When the magnet is pulled out at the same speed, the needle
questions.D: deflects to the right with double the reading
questions.explanation: Lenz's law: the induced current reverses when the direction of motion (change of flux) reverses.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The activity of a radioactive sample falls to one-eighth of its original value in 24 minutes. Its half-life is
questions.explanation: 1/8 = (1/2)³ — three half-lives in 24 minutes ⇒ half-life = 8 minutes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a nucleus emits a beta particle, its
questions.explanation: A neutron becomes a proton and an electron (the beta particle) is emitted: mass number unchanged, atomic number +1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light of frequency 6 × 10¹⁴ Hz falls on a metal whose work function is 2 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Taking h = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A p-n junction diode conducts easily when
questions.A: the p-side is connected to the negative terminal of the battery
questions.C: the p-side is connected to the positive terminal of the battery
questions.explanation: Forward bias (p to positive, n to negative) narrows the depletion layer and allows current to flow.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴. The element
questions.B: has 4 electrons in its outermost shell
questions.explanation: The outer shell 3s² 3p⁴ holds 6 electrons (Group 6); it gains 2 electrons to form X²⁻ (like sulphur).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of species are isotopes?
questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same atomic number) with different mass numbers: ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Elements X, Y and Z have atomic numbers 11, 17 and 18 respectively. The compound most likely formed between X and Y is
questions.explanation: X (2,8,1) is a metal that loses one electron; Y (2,8,7) is a non-metal that gains one; they form the ionic compound XY (like NaCl). Z (2,8,8) is a noble gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ammonia (NH₃) reacts with a hydrogen ion to form the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺. The bond formed between NH₃ and H⁺ is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen donates its lone pair to H⁺, which contributes no electrons — a dative covalent bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which substance conducts electricity in the molten state but not in the solid state?
questions.explanation: Ionic solids have fixed ions; when melted the ions become mobile and conduct. Copper and graphite conduct as solids; sulphur never does.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The volume of 0.5 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid needed to neutralise 2.0 g of sodium hydroxide is (NaOH = 40)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What mass of magnesium oxide is produced when 4.8 g of magnesium burns completely in oxygen? (Mg = 24, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO; n(Mg) = 4.8/24 = 0.2 mol ⇒ 0.2 mol MgO × 40 g/mol = 8.0 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A hydrocarbon contains 85.7% carbon by mass and has a relative molecular mass of 42. Its molecular formula is (C = 12, H = 1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many moles of oxygen atoms are present in 0.5 mol of Al₂(SO₄)₃?
questions.explanation: Each formula unit has 3 × 4 = 12 oxygen atoms; 0.5 × 12 = 6 mol of O atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 2.24 dm³ of a gas at s.t.p. has a mass of 6.4 g. Its relative molecular mass is (molar volume = 22.4 dm³)
questions.explanation: n = 2.24/22.4 = 0.1 mol; M = 6.4/0.1 = 64 (sulphur(IV) oxide, SO₂).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas at 27 °C and 1 atm is heated to 327 °C at constant volume. The new pressure is
questions.explanation: P ∝ T at constant volume: P₂ = 1 × 600/300 = 2 atm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A sealed balloon contains 2 dm³ of air at 1 atm. Its volume when the external pressure falls to 0.8 atm at the same temperature is
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: V₂ = P₁V₁/P₂ = 1 × 2/0.8 = 2.5 dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 20 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide is mixed with 20 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. The pH of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: Equal moles of a strong acid and strong base neutralise completely to give a neutral salt solution, pH 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution has a hydrogen-ion concentration of 1 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³. The solution is
questions.explanation: pH = −log(10⁻⁵) = 5, below 7 but only mildly acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following methods is most suitable for preparing an insoluble salt such as barium tetraoxosulphate(VI)?
questions.C: reaction of a metal with an acid
questions.explanation: Mixing solutions of soluble salts (e.g. BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄) precipitates the insoluble salt, which is filtered off and washed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When a few drops of universal indicator are added to a solution of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV), the colour observed is
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ is a salt of a strong base and weak acid; it hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution (pH ≈ 11).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 2FeCl₂ + Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃, the substance being reduced is
questions.explanation: Chlorine gains electrons (0 → −1); it is reduced and acts as the oxidising agent. Iron is oxidised from +2 to +3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What mass of copper(II) oxide is needed to react completely with 20 cm³ of 2.0 mol/dm³ tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid? (CuO = 80)
questions.explanation: CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O. n(acid) = 2 × 0.02 = 0.04 mol = n(CuO); mass = 0.04 × 80 = 3.2 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A student adds 1 g of powdered zinc to acid and, in a second experiment, 1 g of zinc granules to the same acid. The powdered zinc reacts faster because
questions.A: it has a lower activation energy
questions.D: it has a larger surface area
questions.explanation: Smaller particles expose more surface to the acid, so more successful collisions occur per second.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an energy profile diagram, the products lie at a higher energy level than the reactants. The reaction is
questions.explanation: Energy is absorbed to raise the products above the reactants: ΔH is positive (endothermic).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by
questions.C: providing an alternative path of lower activation energy
questions.D: increasing the energy of the products
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy so that more colliding molecules can react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the equilibrium 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = −196 kJ, the yield of SO₃ is decreased by
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic, so raising the temperature shifts the equilibrium to the left (Le Chatelier).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility of a salt is 20 g per 100 g of water at 30 °C. A solution containing 15 g of the salt in 50 g of water at 30 °C is
questions.explanation: 50 g of water dissolves at most 10 g at 30 °C; 15 g exceeds this, so the solution holds more than saturation — supersaturated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution using carbon electrodes, the product at the anode is
questions.explanation: In concentrated brine, Cl⁻ is discharged in preference to OH⁻ at the anode, giving chlorine; hydrogen forms at the cathode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A current of 2 A flows for 16 minutes 5 seconds through molten aluminium oxide. The mass of aluminium deposited is (Al = 27, F = 96,500 C/mol)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an electrochemical cell the electrode where oxidation occurs is the
questions.explanation: Oxidation always takes place at the anode (An Ox); reduction at the cathode (Red Cat).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A sample of water still forms a scum with soap even after boiling. The hardness is most likely due to
questions.explanation: Permanent hardness, not removed by boiling, is caused by the sulphates and chlorides of calcium and magnesium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The gas mainly responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer is
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that catalyse the breakdown of ozone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Iron is extracted from haematite in the blast furnace. The reducing agent that converts Fe₂O₃ to iron is
questions.explanation: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂; carbon(II) oxide formed from coke is the main reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal is extracted from its molten chloride by electrolysis rather than by reduction with carbon because the metal
questions.C: is a liquid at room temperature
questions.explanation: Metals above carbon in the reactivity series (Na, Ca, Mg, Al) cannot be reduced by carbon and are extracted by electrolysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aluminium does not corrode as readily as iron because
questions.A: aluminium forms a thin, tough oxide layer that protects it
questions.B: aluminium is much lower than iron in the reactivity series
questions.C: aluminium does not react with oxygen or water vapour
questions.D: iron is a transition metal with variable oxidation states
questions.explanation: The adherent Al₂O₃ film seals the surface; iron's rust is porous and flakes off.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The compound CH₃CH₂CH₂OH and CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ are
questions.explanation: Both are C₃H₈O (propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol) with different structures — isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol is dehydrated by passing its vapour over heated aluminium oxide. The product is
questions.explanation: Dehydration removes water: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃ is
questions.explanation: The longest chain has 4 carbons (butane), with a methyl group on carbon 2 when numbered from the end nearest the branch.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When propene is polymerised, the product is
questions.explanation: Addition polymerisation of propene monomers gives poly(propene).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Soap is made by boiling a fat or oil with
questions.explanation: Saponification: fat + NaOH → soap (sodium salt of fatty acids) + glycerol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A food sample turns purple when warmed with sodium hydroxide and a few drops of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution. The food contains
questions.explanation: The biuret test gives a violet/purple colour with proteins (peptide bonds).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Haber process the conditions used are about 450 °C, 200 atm and an iron catalyst. The moderately high temperature is chosen because
questions.A: it gives the highest yield of ammonia
questions.B: it is a compromise between yield and rate of reaction
questions.explanation: Low temperature favours yield (exothermic) but makes the reaction too slow; 450 °C balances yield against speed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The raw materials for the Solvay process for making sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) are
questions.explanation: Brine (NaCl), limestone (for CO₂) and ammonia (recycled) are the Solvay inputs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Going down Group 7 from fluorine to iodine, the elements
questions.explanation: Reactivity of the halogens decreases down the group because the outer shell is farther from the nucleus and gains electrons less readily.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A student observed a thin slice of onion under the microscope and saw cells with a cell wall and nucleus but no chloroplasts. This is because
questions.A: onion cells are animal cells and therefore lack plastids
questions.B: the bulb grows underground and does not photosynthesise
questions.C: the slice was too thin for chloroplasts to be visible
questions.D: chloroplasts are found only in the roots of the onion plant
questions.explanation: Onion bulb scales are underground storage tissue; they have plant cell walls but no chloroplasts because they receive no light.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Using a microscope with a ×10 eyepiece and a ×40 objective, a cell appears 2 mm wide. Its actual width is
questions.explanation: Total magnification = 10 × 40 = 400; actual size = image size/magnification = 2/400 = 0.005 mm.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An organism is single-celled, has no true nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles. It belongs to the kingdom
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes (bacteria and blue-green algae) lack a true nucleus and are placed in Monera.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A plant has parallel-veined leaves, fibrous roots and flower parts in threes. It is most likely
questions.explanation: Parallel venation, fibrous roots and trimerous flowers are monocot features (e.g. maize, grasses).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A patient is unable to digest fats properly after the removal of the gall bladder because
questions.A: the body can no longer produce any lipase at all
questions.B: bile that emulsifies fats can no longer be stored and released in quantity
questions.C: the stomach can no longer churn fatty food properly
questions.D: the pancreas stops secreting its digestive juices
questions.explanation: The gall bladder stores bile; bile salts emulsify fats into droplets so that lipase can act on them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A child has bow legs and a deformed chest. The child most likely lacks
questions.explanation: Rickets, with soft, bent bones, results from a deficiency of vitamin D and calcium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A child has a swollen belly, thin limbs and reddish hair. The condition is most likely
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency: oedema (swollen belly), wasted muscles and discoloured hair.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In an experiment, a test tube containing starch solution and saliva was kept at 37 °C. After 20 minutes, iodine solution gave no blue-black colour. This shows that
questions.A: the starch had been converted to sugar by salivary amylase
questions.B: iodine does not react with starch at 37 °C
questions.explanation: Amylase in saliva hydrolyses starch to maltose at body temperature, so no starch is left to react with iodine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The same starch-saliva experiment was repeated with the saliva first boiled. Iodine turned blue-black. This is because boiling
questions.A: increased the activity of the enzyme too much
questions.B: denatured the enzyme, so the starch was not digested
questions.C: converted all the starch directly into glucose
questions.D: made the iodine solution more concentrated
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins; boiling changes their shape permanently (denaturation) and they stop working.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A leafy shoot was placed in water containing red dye. After some hours, a cross-section of the stem showed red colour only in certain tissues. Those tissues were
questions.explanation: Water and dissolved substances move up the plant through xylem vessels, which the dye stained.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A ring of bark (containing phloem) was removed from around a tree trunk. After some weeks the bark above the ring swelled because
questions.A: water from the roots accumulated above the ring
questions.B: sugars moving down from the leaves could not pass the ring
questions.C: the xylem vessels became blocked at the ring
questions.D: the roots sent extra food upwards to heal the wound
questions.explanation: Ringing removes phloem; food translocated downwards from the leaves accumulates above the cut.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person's red blood cell count is low and the cells are small and pale. The person most likely lacks
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; its shortage causes iron-deficiency anaemia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Blood leaving the lungs through the pulmonary vein is
questions.A: deoxygenated and goes to the right atrium
questions.B: oxygenated and goes to the left atrium
questions.C: oxygenated and goes to the right ventricle
questions.D: deoxygenated and goes to the left ventricle
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood; it enters the left atrium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two flasks of germinating seeds were set up; the seeds in the second flask were first boiled. A thermometer in the first flask showed a rise in temperature, the second showed none. This shows that
questions.A: boiled seeds respire faster than living seeds
questions.B: living seeds release heat during respiration
questions.C: boiling stores extra heat inside the seeds
questions.D: germinating seeds absorb heat from the air
questions.explanation: Respiration releases energy, some as heat; killed (boiled) seeds do not respire.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When a person breathes out, the diaphragm
questions.explanation: Expiration: the diaphragm relaxes and rises, the ribs fall, chest volume decreases and air is forced out.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Yeast added to a sugar solution in a warm place produces bubbles of gas and a smell of alcohol. The process is
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments glucose to ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide in the absence of oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Glucose was found in a patient's urine. This suggests a problem with
questions.A: the kidney's ability to reabsorb glucose or with insulin production
questions.B: the liver's production and storage of bile
questions.C: the exchange of gases in the lungs
questions.D: the sweat glands and the control of body temperature
questions.explanation: Normally all glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule; excess blood glucose (diabetes) overwhelms reabsorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: On a cold day a person passes more dilute urine than on a hot day because
questions.A: the kidneys filter blood much faster in cold weather
questions.B: less water is lost as sweat, so less ADH is released and less water is reabsorbed
questions.C: the bladder expands and holds more urine in cold weather
questions.D: more cold water is drunk, which the kidneys cannot absorb
questions.explanation: With less sweating the blood is more dilute; ADH secretion falls and the kidney tubules reabsorb less water.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A plant left unwatered wilts because
questions.A: its xylem vessels collapse and can no longer carry water
questions.B: its cells lose turgor as water leaves the vacuoles
questions.C: its cell walls dissolve once water is no longer available
questions.D: photosynthesis stops and the leaves no longer make food
questions.explanation: Turgor pressure supports soft tissues; when water is short the cells become flaccid and the plant droops.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The hinge joint at the elbow allows movement
questions.explanation: Hinge joints (elbow, knee) permit bending and straightening in one plane; ball-and-socket joints move in all directions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A flower has brightly coloured petals, a strong scent, nectar and sticky pollen grains. It is adapted for pollination by
questions.explanation: Colour, scent and nectar attract insects; sticky pollen clings to their bodies.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In humans, the fusion of a sperm carrying a Y chromosome with an ovum produces
questions.explanation: The ovum always carries X; X + Y gives a male (XY).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The part of the mammalian female reproductive system where fertilisation normally takes place is the
questions.explanation: Sperm meet the ovum in the oviduct; the zygote then travels to the uterus to implant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A germinating bean seed was marked with ink lines at equal intervals along the radicle. After two days the lines just behind the tip were farthest apart. This shows that
questions.A: growth occurs equally along the root
questions.B: the region of elongation lies just behind the root tip
questions.C: the root tip does not grow
questions.explanation: Cells produced at the tip (meristem) elongate in the zone just behind it, spreading the marks.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Seeds soaked in water and kept in a warm, dark, airy cupboard germinated, while identical seeds kept in a refrigerator did not. The experiment shows that germination requires
questions.explanation: Both sets had water and air; only the temperature differed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A boy walking from bright sunlight into a dim room cannot see clearly at first. During this time his
questions.A: pupils constrict to protect the retina
questions.B: pupils dilate to admit more light
questions.C: lenses become thinner to focus on near objects
questions.D: corneas thicken to gather more light
questions.explanation: The iris reflex widens the pupil in dim light; adjustment takes a few moments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A person with goitre (swollen neck) most likely has a deficiency of
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland enlarges when it cannot make enough thyroxine for lack of iodine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A student frightened by a snake finds her heart racing and her mouth dry. The hormone responsible is
questions.explanation: Adrenaline, from the adrenal glands, prepares the body for 'fight or flight'.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a pond, small fish eat water fleas which feed on algae; herons eat the fish. The organisms with the greatest total biomass are the
questions.explanation: Energy is lost at each trophic level, so producers (algae) have the greatest biomass in a normal pyramid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Lichens growing on a bare rock surface are an example of
questions.A: climax vegetation in a stable community
questions.C: parasites feeding on the minerals in rock
questions.D: secondary succession after a forest fire
questions.explanation: Lichens colonise bare rock first, breaking it down to form soil for later communities.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A tapeworm lives in the intestine of a man, absorbing digested food and causing him harm. The relationship is
questions.explanation: One organism benefits at the expense of the living host — parasitism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Bacteria in the root nodules of legumes fix nitrogen for the plant and receive sugars in return. This relationship is
questions.explanation: Both partners benefit — mutualism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Two equal samples of soil were heated: sample A lost 15% of its mass, sample B lost 3%. Sample A most likely contains more
questions.explanation: Strong heating burns off organic matter; the greater loss shows more humus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A farmer notices that his crops grow poorly in a waterlogged field. The main reason is that
questions.B: the roots lack oxygen for respiration
questions.explanation: Waterlogging fills air spaces; roots cannot respire and nutrient uptake fails.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Repeated spraying of a farm with the same insecticide became less effective after a few years because
questions.explanation: Natural selection: the few resistant insects survive each spraying and pass on their resistance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The main reason why farmers practise crop rotation with legumes is that legumes
questions.A: need very little water and survive drought
questions.B: add nitrogen to the soil through root-nodule bacteria
questions.C: have deep roots that break up hard soil
questions.D: grow quickly and shade out weeds
questions.explanation: Rhizobium in legume nodules fixes atmospheric nitrogen, enriching the soil for the next crop.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A man with blood group A (genotype IᴬIᴼ) marries a woman with blood group B (IᴮIᴼ). The percentage of their children expected to have blood group O is
questions.explanation: Gametes Iᴬ, i × Iᴮ, i give IᴬIᴮ, Iᴬi, Iᴮi, ii — one in four (25%) is ii (group O).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of discontinuous variation in humans?
questions.explanation: Tongue rolling is either present or absent (discrete classes); height, mass and skin colour vary continuously.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A haemophiliac man marries a woman who is not a carrier. Their sons will be
questions.explanation: Sons receive the Y chromosome from the father and a normal X from the mother; they are all normal. Daughters will all be carriers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The forelimbs of a bat, a whale and a man have the same basic bone structure but different functions. This is evidence of evolution from
questions.explanation: Homologous structures share a common origin, suggesting a common ancestor.
